glossary.headline: Different terms.
glossary.lede: Specialized knowledge. Practical ability. Pride in the work.

items.def: Occupations centered on specialized practical skills, technical knowledge, and hands-on work—such as welding, electrical work, HVAC, carpentry, and masonry.
A broader economic term for workers with specialized training, knowledge, or experience. Skilled trades are one part of this wider category.
The care, judgment, precision, and practiced ability behind quality work. Craftsmanship is visible in how a tradesperson plans, executes, and finishes a task.

Careers developed through applied education and occupational training, including technical schools, trade schools, apprenticeships, and employer programs. Educational routes can overlap with college study.

items.a: No. Our vision uses VR to prepare for and reinforce instructor-led learning. Real tools, supervised shop work, and practical assessment remain essential.

items.q: Can I earn a license or certification here?
items.a: This website introduces the XVR Trade Skills vision and offers career exploration. It does not award credentials. Check requirements with the relevant training provider, licensing authority, or certifying organization.

items.q: Which products can I purchase today?
items.a: Very affordable access is a core commitment of XVR Trade Skills. Specific prices, packages, product availability, and technical requirements are not published here yet. The trade experiences illustrate our educational direction.
